headline: Highest risk is broad network egress plus shared automation surfaces creating medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can ingest task outputs and external content in automation flows, while EMQX exposes an HTTP API and broad network egress. No shared channel is documented, but the pair can be bridged through files or messages in default deployments, so injection is plausible and not blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF Airflow tasks consume EMQX-delivered payloads as instructions or templates
IF a shared filesystem, queue, or HTTP endpoint bridges the two agents
IF operators copy EMQX output into Airflow DAG inputs without sanitization
mitigations: Add strict content-type validation on all EMQX-to-Airflow payloads
Disable any automatic parsing of free-form text as commands
Use separate queues or folders with provenance labels
Require manual review before promoting external content into DAGs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and EMQX touches IoT data. Airflow does not list data classes, but its orchestration role can move file or message contents across boundaries. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default automation setups, though direct shared storage is not documented, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF Airflow workflows read IoT payloads from EMQX and forward them to external services
IF both agents share a workspace, bucket, or message bus
IF EMQX outputs are logged or exported without redaction
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate storage namespaces
Review outbound destinations for both agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is a data orchestrator and EMQX is a broker with HTTP API access; both have broad network egress, so they can contend over shared mutable resources such as queues, topics, or downstream APIs. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so overlapping writes are plausible and medium severity fits.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same downstream API or topic
IF Airflow retries collide with EMQX-delivered updates
IF a shared database or object store is used without locks
mitigations: Set retry backoff to reduce collisions

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can operationalize outputs from other systems, and EMQX can emit IoT data over HTTP APIs. If Airflow treats EMQX-derived data as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream jobs or alerts. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the interaction is plausible and not safely bounded.
conditions: IF Airflow schedules actions directly from EMQX messages
IF EMQX payloads are used as facts without validation
IF downstream jobs execute on unverified sensor or broker data
mitigations: Insert schema validation before Airflow actions
Require human approval for high-impact jobs
Compare EMQX data against a second source
Log and alert on parsing failures

E_compliance.rationale: EMQX explicitly touches IoT data, while Airflow's profile does not specify regulated data classes or residency. No concrete residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern is supportable. The other agent is not cited beyond its generic orchestration role because the evidence is one-sided.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is routed through EMQX into Airflow logs
IF retention policies differ between the two systems
IF a jurisdictional residency rule applies to the IoT payloads
mitigations: Document data residency for each pipeline
